transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I'm here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart lately. I'll lie in bed in my apartment for hours with my laptop closed, but I'm still mentally rechecking work deadlines, tuition payments, and class assignments. It's just constant. And even when I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off.
How long has this pattern of racing thoughts and poor sleep been going on?

It's been about a year and three months now. It pretty much started right when I began an evening graduate certificate program, since I'm doing that while trying to keep up with my full-time job as an analyst.
Over this same period, have you noticed feeling persistently down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I don't think I've felt sad or down. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted all the time, but I still care about the things I usually enjoy. It's more just... being too wound up or tired to actually do them, rather than losing interest in them.
Aside from when you're trying to fall asleep, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about work, school, or other things throughout the day?

Yeah, it's pretty much all day long. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to the next. I'll worry about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then that turns into worrying if I'm just wasting my money on school... and then I start stressing about whether my family will think I can't handle everything. It's like I treat every single small issue that comes up like it could completely derail my whole future.
Do you often notice physical tension, like tight muscles, or feel restless and on edge, separate from your sleep difficulties?

I haven't really noticed that, to be honest. I mean, I don't think my muscles get particularly tight or anything like that. I don't really feel physically restless or on edge during the day... it's more just the mental exhaustion from my mind racing all the time. But physically, no, I haven't really felt what you're describing.
When you're lying awake, do you find yourself specifically worrying about not being able to fall asleep or about the sleep loss itself, separate from your worries about work and school?

No, not really. I mean, I know I'm not sleeping, and that's frustrating, but the sleep itself isn't what I'm focused on. It's more that lying there in the quiet just gives my brain a chance to run through all those other things... the work stuff, school, my family. I don't really lay there stressing about the fact that I'm awake. I'm just awake because I'm stressing about everything else.
